newsitem.title: FRANCE: Solana hopes NATO-Russia text ready at July summit.
newsitem.headline: Solana hopes NATO-Russia text ready at July summit.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said on Friday that what he called a binding text governing relations between the alliance and Moscow could be ready for signing at a Madrid summit in July.
Solana told the French newspaper Le Figaro in an interview that the text would "obviously be politically binding" but gave no details.

The United States has rejected Moscow's demand for a full legally binding charter regulating relations and allowing Russia veto rights in some areas of policy. It seems likely the Kremlin will settle for something falling short of such a deal but acknowledging Russian interests.

"We are ready to sign as soon as the other party wishes. But we obviously want to finish in time for the NATO summit in July in Madrid, which among other tasks must designate countries which we will invite to join," Solana said.
"I will do my best so that everything is ready for Madrid," he added.
Solana said his talks in Brussels at the weekend with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov had been constructive and that he planned to pursue them with a visit to Moscow late next week.
"There is hope, but our positions still diverge greatly on certain points. NATO's military infrastructures for example -- Russia refuses that they be deployed on the territory of new members.
"That shows a lack of understanding of what NATO really is: most of the infrastructures are national and are not dependent on the alliance," Solana said.
